action_taken: the dental chair unit was thoroughly inspected. water droplets were observed coming from the air rotors even when the foot switch was released. the handpieces were individually examined and found to be functioning properly. upon further inspection, the wrv (water regulation valve) was identified as the cause of the issue. the valve was unable to fully stop the water flow due to a spring mechanism being stuck as a result of accumulated debris. the valve assembly was cleaned, debris removed, and the spring mechanism lubricated. after servicing, the system was tested and confirmed to be operating normally. no water leakage was observed from the air rotors.

fault_description: the flow rate could not be increased beyond 4 lpm.
action_taken: the bubble cpap system was inspected and it was observed that adequate bubbling was not occurring. further assessment revealed leakage in the patient breathing circuit. in addition, the water level in the bubble chamber was found to be above the recommended maximum level, causing water overflow and affecting proper pressure and flow generation. the patient circuit connections were secured correctly to eliminate leakage. excess water from the bubble chamber was drained and the water level was adjusted to the recommended range. after corrective actions, proper bubbling was observed and the flow rate could be increased beyond 4 lpm without difficulty. user training was provided to the nursing staff regarding correct circuit connections, proper water level maintenance, and routine handling of the bubble cpap system.
